problem: The qualification gate required verified fault-service attestation from campaign evidence, but crash-retry intentionally terminates the fault service before a response can be returned. The existing dual-service preflight also did not verify Ed25519 response attestations, so end-to-end fault-service provenance could not be proven.

reviews.preferred: attested dual-service read-only preflight plus separate campaign attestation evidence
reviews.reason: The fault endpoint can safely prove identity on stats without weakening crash-after-commit semantics. Campaign responses still prove the normal execution path.

reviews.preferred: verify signatures at the transport boundary and pass normalized verified evidence into qualification
reviews.reason: This keeps the coordinator private key outside the worker and prevents worker-declared service names from becoming authority.

reviews.preferred: reuse the existing normal/fault preflight calls
reviews.reason: No new qrexec round trips are added beyond the already-required dual preflight, and production mission semantics remain unchanged.

alternatives.name: require fault attestation from crash_retry
alternatives.reason: Impossible by design when the fault service terminates before writing a response.

alternatives.name: inject synthetic attestation events into campaign JSONL
alternatives.reason: Would blur campaign framing and make provenance easier to spoof or misinterpret.

alternatives.name: add a third attestation daemon/service
alternatives.reason: Adds lifecycle, policy, resource, and regression surface without improving this stage enough to justify it.

expected_effects.correctness: Qualification can now prove both services without contradicting crash-injection behavior.
expected_effects.robustness: Missing or mismatched key, SHA, or service identity fails closed before campaigns.
expected_effects.latency: No additional qrexec calls beyond existing dual preflight.
expected_effects.resources: Negligible local signature verification and evidence validation overhead.
expected_effects.regression_risk: Low; changes are limited to qualification/preflight evidence handling and tests.

lessons: A fault endpoint designed to die cannot be required to produce post-fault response evidence.
Preflight identity evidence and campaign execution evidence are different evidence classes and should remain explicitly separated.
Cryptographic primitives do not improve readiness unless the final evaluator consumes their verified output.
